snippet.title: Ancient Rome: The Original Megacity
snippet.description:

In this video, I use AI to reconstruct Ancient Rome at its absolute peak. 

The Colosseum. 
The Pantheon. 
The Roman Forum. 
Trajan's Market. 
The aqueducts that brought 190,000 cubic meters of water daily. 
The insulae apartment buildings where 90% of Romans lived.

This is the city that invented the modern metropolis. 
The place that solved the impossible problem of making 1 million people work in one place.
See Rome as Romans saw it.

snippet.title: Boston - 1700s
snippet.description:
Journey through pre-Revolutionary Boston, a city on the brink of dramatic change in American history. From a crowded colonial port to the streets, taverns, and meeting halls that shaped resistance, this exploration reveals a city defined by trade, tension, and everyday life on the edge of revolution.

Using modern AI video tools and original 18th-century paintings, maps, and engravings, this video reconstructs Boston as it existed before independence with striking realism. By reimagining period artwork and historical records, we bring the scale, atmosphere, and character of colonial Boston back to life — allowing us to move through the city as it once was, and to compare these historic locations with how they appear today.

snippet.title: The American Revolution
snippet.description:
How did a tax dispute become a war, and how did a war become a nation? This documentary tells the complete story of the American Revolution from 1765 to 1789. Watch as British colonial policies push Americans to rebellion, as the first shots at Lexington explode into eight years of warfare across two continents. Experience the major battles—Bunker Hill, Trenton, Saratoga, Yorktown—and see what happened after: the Treaty of Paris, Washington's historic resignation, and the Constitutional Convention that built a republic from the ashes of war.

This reconstruction aims to reflect that world — historically grounded and visually reimagined.

snippet.title: Paris - 1600s
snippet.description:
Step into the grandeur of 17th-century Paris with an AI-generated reconstruction, inspired by the meticulous engravings, painted cityscapes, and architectural plans created throughout the early reign of Louis XIV. This visualisation draws heavily from the works of Jacques Callot, Israel Silvestre, and other court-appointed artists whose observational drawings captured Paris as it transformed into the political and cultural heart of France. All historical details are interpreted using AI for cinematic presentation, but great care has been taken to remain faithful to the colours, materials, and spatial character of Paris as it appeared at the time.

During this century, Paris was undergoing extraordinary change. Streets were widened, new bridges and quays were built along the Seine, and monumental projects began to reflect the growing power of the Bourbon monarchy. By mid-century, under the guidance of Louis XIV and his ministers, the city shifted from its medieval fabric toward a more ordered, classical vision — a process that would accelerate after 1661 when Louis took direct control of the state.

Artists like Silvestre documented this evolving metropolis in lavish detail: the Louvre still partly medieval but expanding toward its classical façades; the Île de la Cité alive with markets and churches; the Marais rising as the district of nobles; and the newly completed Place Royale (now Place des Vosges) standing as an early symbol of royal urban planning.

One of the most influential visual records from this era is Israel Silvestre’s panoramic Paris engravings, produced during his tenure as Louis XIV’s official court draughtsman. Although not always perfectly measured — perspectives were sometimes adjusted, alignments idealised, and architectural details refined to emphasize harmony — these works remain unmatched as windows into the pre-Haussmann, pre-Revolutionary city.

This reconstruction seeks to echo that spirit: historically grounded, artistically interpreted, and dedicated to showing Paris just as it stood on the threshold of becoming the great capital of Louis XIV’s France.

snippet.title: Greatest Speech in American History?
snippet.description:
This video presents an AI reconstruction of Abraham Lincoln’s Gettysburg Address, recreated with care to honor its historical legacy.
Using advanced voice and audio modeling, the speech is brought to life in a way modern audiences can experience firsthand.
The setting and tone aim to reflect the solemn atmosphere of the original 1863 ceremony.
This reconstruction does not alter the message, but seeks to preserve the emotional weight of the moment.
Viewers are invited to imagine the crowd, the battlefield, and the nation struggling to hold together.
The video highlights how a brief speech became a defining symbol of American purpose.
It reminds us that even in times of division, clarity and conviction can guide a nation forward.
This is a respectful tribute to a timeless turning point in American history.

localized.title: Edinburgh - 1700s
localized.description:
Step into Edinburgh before the New Town, when the city was dense, defensive, and shaped by centuries of pressure. This video explores 18th-century Edinburgh through its streets, landmarks, and hidden edges — from the castle rock and crowded High Street to vanished features like the Nor Loch. Using modern AI tools and historic paintings, maps, and engravings, the past is reconstructed in motion, allowing us to move through these scenes and experience the city as it once was. Stay until the end to see how these same places compare to Edinburgh today.

snippet.title: 10 Amazing Buildings That Once Were!
snippet.description:
Some buildings survive for thousands of years. Others - just as magnificent, just as important - disappear completely. In this video, I use AI to reconstruct 10 of history's most legendary lost structures. From Shakespeare's Globe Theatre to the fortress that sparked the French Revolution, these buildings shaped the world... then vanished. Discover what they looked like, why they mattered, and how they were destroyed. History you can finally see again.

snippet.title: New York - 1600s
snippet.description:
Step into 17th-century New York with an AI reconstruction inspired by colonial maps, traveler accounts, and early Dutch and English city plans. Using records from the Dutch West India Company, English surveyors, and contemporary sketches, this visualisation interprets the settlement’s shift from New Amsterdam to New York while staying true to its materials and street patterns.

During this century, the town changed quickly: timber houses lined Pearl Street, Fort Amsterdam guarded the harbor, and the defensive Wall—later Wall Street—marked its edge. Even after the 1664 English takeover, Dutch architecture and customs remained visible.

Though imperfect, early maps and drawings reveal a frontier port of muddy streets, active docks, and a mix of Dutch, English, African, and Native residents. This reconstruction aims to reflect that world as New York stood on the threshold of becoming a major Atlantic city.
